newsitem.title: USA: Abercrombie & Fitch IPO set to make a splash. [CORRECTED 21:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Abercrombie & Fitch IPO set to make a splash. [CORRECTED 21:30 GMT]

text.p: Abercrombie & Fitch Co's casual wear brand strength and its consistent earnings growth have made it one of the jewels in the Limited Inc's $7.9 billion retail empire, and investors are likely to snap up its stock at its market debut this week.

Abercrombie's established name, the success of other niche retail IPOs, and a resurgent enthusiasm for IPOs should combine to make the 7.0 million (corrects from 7.8 million) share deal a coveted one.
"This is hot, hot, hot," said John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket newsletter.

Shares of the Reynoldsville, Ohio-based company are expected to make their debut later this week at an estimated price range of $14-$16 per share. Lead underwriter Goldman, Sachs is offering the shares.

Analysts expect the stock to immediately move above its offering price. Fitzgibbon said growing demand for the deal means it could outstrip initial expectations of a two to three point premium at the opening.

Growth prospects look promising, say analysts. Mark Basham, new issues analyst at Standard & Poor's, said "the company should be able to continue its excellent growth record. We expect earnings growth to equal or exceed 30 percent over the next four years."
The company reported 1995 sales of $235.7 million, up 42 percent from 1994 sales of $165.5 million.
Its same store sales rose five percent in the soft retail market of 1995, while same store sales for the Limited fell two percent in the same period.

The Limited bought Abercrombie & Fitch from Oshman's Sporting Goods Inc in 1988. In recent years, Abercrombie has outperformed most of the Limited's other units including Limited Express and Limited Too.

Its IPO is expected to outshine that of its sister unit last year. Intimate Brands Inc, parent of Victoria's Secret, went public in October and has risen only about 10 percent from its IPO price of $17.

Manish Shah, editor and publisher of the IPO Maven, said he expects demand for niche retail stocks to boost Abercrombie's stock to an opening "around 20 percent higher than the offer price,". He cited the opening success of other niche retail IPOs, including Loehmann's Inc and Hot Topic - a specialty apparel company which jumped 60 percent on its first day of trading on Tuesday.

The Abercrombie & Fitch brand name has been renowned for its durable, rugged, outdoor raiment since 1892, but since 1992 the company has been repositioning itself to appeal to a more youthful, fashion-conscious audience.

Shah sees further widening of its product line required in the long run. He said the stock would probably settle at around $23 to $24, and that it "won't really go higher unless (they) broaden the customer base".

Terrence McEvoy, retail analyst at Janney Montgomery Scott, agrees that this may be a good idea in the long-run. "Gap went beyond its traditional base .... Abercrombie may have to do something similar somewhere down the road".
For the time being, though, he said he "assumes there will be strong interest" in the retailer's stock.
Mark Basham said he sees Abercrombie's clothes as "having a broad appeal. And they are expanding the product line - that will bring more people in the store."
After the IPO, Limited will own about 95 percent of Abercrombie's voting power.
